questions.q: Why are specific goals more effective than telling yourself to do your best?
a: They give you a concrete standard to measure progress against
They make the task feel less intimidating to start
They remove the need for short-term goals
They rely on external rewards rather than willpower
questions.why: The summary says vague goals offer nothing concrete to track your growth against.

questions.q: What specific goal helped Bar-Eli pass his 3,000-meter run?
a: Keeping up with the runners at the front of the pack
Finishing the run in under ten minutes
Beating his own previous best time
Training every morning before breakfast
questions.why: With a clear target, he achieved something he had not managed before.

questions.q: What did Dick Fosbury do differently from other high jumpers?
a: He jumped backward over the bar instead of leaping frontward
He used a longer run-up than anyone else
He jumped from a standing position
He trained with a heavier bar
questions.why: His unorthodox flop won him a gold medal and became the standard technique.

questions.q: What four steps does the summary give for turning an idea into an innovation?
a: Realize the problem, find an unexpected solution, practice it, share it
Research the market, raise money, build a team, launch
Copy a rival, cut the price, advertise widely, expand
Set a goal, visualize success, measure results, repeat
questions.why: Fosbury followed this pattern from his struggle with the straddle roll to Olympic gold.

questions.q: What should visualization focus on, according to the summary?
a: The sensory details of the process, not just the outcome
The applause and rewards that follow success
The mistakes you want to avoid making
The speed at which you complete each step
questions.why: Pete Maravich focused on technique rather than watching the ball go in.
